description: How tarot grew from a fifteenth-century Italian card game into the deck used for tarot spread readings, from Visconti-Sforza to Rider-Waite-Smith.
lede: Tarot began as a card game in northern Italy. Its use for reading came centuries later.

timeline.alt: A horizontal timeline of tarot with seven dates: 1440s, first tarot cards in northern Italy; 1500s, the name tarocchi in use; 1700s, the Marseille pattern in France; 1781, Court de Gébelin's Egypt claim; 1783, Etteilla's guide to tarot fortune telling; 1909, the Rider-Waite-Smith deck; and today.
timeline.caption: Key dates in tarot's history. The early dates are approximate, because few records survive.

pack.alt: Diagram of the standard 78-card tarot pack. Four suit cards labelled Wands, Cups, Swords and Pentacles, 14 cards each, make 56 suit cards. A stack of 21 numbered trumps and The Fool make 22 major arcana. 56 plus 22 equals 78 cards.
pack.caption: The standard 78-card tarot pack: 56 suit cards, 21 numbered trumps and The Fool.

game-to-reading.alt: Three panels with arrows between them showing how tarot's use changed. Card game, 1440s to 1700s. Occult interpretation, 1780s to 1800s. Reading and reflection, 1900s to today.
game-to-reading.caption: Three stages in tarot's use: first a card game, then an object of occult theory, then a tool for reading and reflection.
